title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is constructing the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space X. The strata X_i are indexed by a finite poset I; X_i is the closed stratum and X_i^* the open one. A strictly increasing 'dimension function' δ: I → ℕ is fixed, and X_(d) = ∪_{δ(i)≤d} X_i is the closed skeleton filtration. The goal, announced on the previous page, is a decreasing filtration by closed sets X = X^(0) ⊃ X^(1) ⊃ … ⊃ X^(N+1) = ∅ with X^(d) ⊂ X \ X_(d-1). It is obtained by successively removing open tubular neighbourhoods of the skeleta, so that each stratum is replaced by a compact 'core' Σ_i: a manifold with corners sitting inside the open stratum X_i^*.

Step 1. Choose a standard tubular neighbourhood T_(0) of X_(0) in X. Set X^(1) = X \ T°_(0), X^(1)_(d) = X^(1) ∩ X_(d) (empty for d ≤ 0) and X^(1)_i = X^(1) ∩ X_i. Then X^(1)_(d) = ∪_{δ(i)≤d} X^(1) ∩ X_i, so X^(1) inherits a stratification with the bottom skeleton removed.

Step 2. Take a standard tubular neighbourhood T_1 of X_(1) in X, chosen small relative to T_0. Its trace T_1^(1) on X^(1) is a standard tubular neighbourhood of X^(1)_(1) in X^(1). Set X^(2) = X^(1) \ T°^(1)_(1) = X^(1) ∩ (X \ T°_1) = X \ (T°_0 ∪ T°_1).

Marginal note ('OPS' = probably 'on peut supposer'): one may assume T_d = ∪_{δ(i)≤d} T_i, where T_i is a tubular neighbourhood of the individual stratum X_i in X. This is the Thom–Mather picture of control data: one tube per stratum, not one per skeleton.

Induction. Take T_d, a tubular neighbourhood of X_(d), small with respect to the T_{d'} already built (d' < d), and set X^(d) = X − ∪_{α<d} T°_α.

Core of each stratum. For i ∈ I with d = δ(i), set Σ_i = X_i ∩ X^(d) = X_i \ ∪_{α<d} X_i ∩ T°_α = X_i − ∪_{j<i} X_i ∩ T°_j ⊂ X_i^*. So Σ_i is the stratum with open tubes around all lower adjacent strata removed: a compact manifold with corners, homotopy equivalent to X_i^*.

What follows (next page). Σ_ij = ∂T_i ∩ Σ_j for i < j, and for flags Σ_{i0…in} = ∂T_{i0} ∩ … ∩ ∂T_{i(n-1)} ∩ Σ_{in}. Inclusions Σ_ij → Σ_j are canonical. The maps Σ_ij → Σ_i come from the tube retractions and should be fibrations under local-triviality ('équisingularité') hypotheses. This produces the combinatorial-topological model of the stratified space: a diagram of compact manifolds with corners indexed by flags of I, as advertised in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (the 'dévissage' theorem).
errors: Notational drift: T_(0) vs T_0, T_1^(1) vs T^(1)_(1), and X^(d) vs X_(d). In (59) the first expression appears as 'X_i ∩ X_(d)'. It must be X_i ∩ X^(d) (superscript), as the following equality shows; X_i ∩ X_(d) would just be X_i.

The equality ∪_{α<d} X_i ∩ T°_α = ∪_{j<i} X_i ∩ T°_j is not automatic. It needs T_α = ∪_{δ(j)≤α} T_j (the marginal 'OPS'). It also needs the tubes T_j of strata not in the closure of X_i (j not < i) to be chosen small enough to miss X_i. This is implicit in 'petit par rapport à' but not stated.

The claim that the trace T_1^(1) of a standard tube T_1 on X^(1) is again a standard tube of X^(1)_(1) in X^(1) requires compatibility of T_1 with ∂T_0. That is, T_0 and T_1 must commute in the Thom–Mather sense (control conditions π_0∘π_1 = π_0, ρ_0∘π_1 = ρ_0). Grothendieck only says 'petit par rapport au choix de T_0'; smallness alone does not give this. The next page acknowledges that equisingularity / local-triviality hypotheses are needed.

Equation numbering is inconsistent: the previous page ends at (47) and the next starts at (49). The labels read '(58)', '(59)' here are probably (48) and an overwritten (48bis)/(49). The first two displayed systems have crossed-out labels.

ideas.what: Inductive removal of open tubular neighbourhoods of the skeleta X_(d), giving a decreasing filtration X^(d) and compact cores Σ_i ⊂ X_i^* of the strata.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution / unfolding of a Thom–Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners (blow-up of strata, 'unzipping')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969) and Mather (1970, control data); Verona (1984, resolution of abstract stratified spaces); Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (dépliage, 1990s); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012, iterated fibration structures); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on 'dévissage' of stratified structures (sketched only, without construction)

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhood of a skeleton taken as the union of tubes of the individual strata, each chosen small relative to earlier ones.
ideas.modern_name: Thom–Mather control data / system of tubular neighbourhoods

ideas.what: Strictly increasing 'dimension function' δ on the poset of strata, used to order the induction.
ideas.modern_name: Depth/dimension filtration of a stratified space

ideas.what: (Continued on next page) Flag-indexed diagram Σ_{i0…in} = ∂T_{i0} ∩ … ∩ Σ_{in}, with canonical inclusions and choice-dependent fibrations Σ_ij → Σ_i.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of links over the subdivision of the stratification poset; model for the exit-path ∞-category / exodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson / Treumann (exit paths); Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; Haine; Barwick–Glasman–Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (as an announced equivalence between stratified spaces and such systems)

missed.claim: The page and its continuation build an explicit diagram of compact manifolds with corners indexed by flags of the stratification poset. Canonical maps exist for inclusions of flags, but the full functoriality is only up to choices of retractions. This is a strict, point-set precursor of the modern statement that a conically stratified space is equivalent to a functor on the exit-path ∞-category, presented over the subdivision sd(I). Grothendieck's 'déploiement' notes appear to anticipate the unzipping construction of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka and the Verona/ALMP resolution, but these manuscripts are not cited in that literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only: the construction itself is now standard. The detailed manuscript could document that the Esquisse 'dévissage theorem' had a concrete Thom–Mather-style construction behind it.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, somewhat sloppy write-up of the standard Thom–Mather inductive removal of tubular neighbourhoods. Its aim, the dévissage of stratified spaces into manifolds with corners, was announced in Esquisse d'un programme and later developed independently by Verona, ALMP, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka and others. Nothing here goes beyond the known theory.

Equation labels read '(58)', '(59)' are likely (48) and an overwritten (48bis)/(49), given the neighbouring numbering (47) and (49). The two earlier displays carry crossed-out labels.
Marginal note: 'OPS T_d = ∪_{i∈I, δ(i)≤d} T_(i), T_i = vois. tub. de X_i dans X'. 'OPS' presumably means 'on peut supposer'.
Second line: 'X^(2) = X^(1) \ T°^(1)_(1) = X^(1) ∩ (X \ T°_1) = X \ (T°_0 ∪ T°_1)'. The image writes 'X^(1)' with a stray symbol in the last line.
In (59) the union in the final expression is over j < i (underlined in the image), with ∂ vs interior written as T°_j.
